That was quite a road statement in the SEC by Keelon Russell and the Alabama offense.The Crimson Tide's 56-23 thumping against previously unbeaten Mississippi State should answer any lingering questions about Alabama's status as a College Football Playoff title contender this season.Updated bowl and College Football Playoff projections after Week 5 feature a surging Alabama team setting the pace in college football's most unforgiving conference, alongside Georgia, who will meet the Crimson Tide next week. The SEC holds two of the projected top four seeds, which doesn't include top-ranked Texas, a reminder that its contenders are jockeying for first-round byes while trying to survive the weekly grind.Ask previously unbeaten Florida about its unforgiving reality check at Missouri.
October has barely arrived, but the stakes already feel like November. Elsewhere, postseason destinations continue to shift as contenders separate themselves and preseason favorites lose ground. Here's where the bowl picture stands nearing the midseason point across college football.We've updated our playoff bracket projections and full list of bowl games after Week 5. A couple of new teams entered our postseason lookahead, and there are major changes within the CFP top 12.Cricket CelebrationProjection: South Carolina State vs. Alabama StateSalute to VeteransProjection: Kennesaw State vs. Old DominionFrisco Football ClassicProjection: WKU vs. Louisiana TechBoca Raton Projection: Boise State vs. MinnesotaGasparillaProjection: Florida State vs. USFNew to this week's bowl projections is Mike Norvell's Seminoles after a 31-point backhand of Virginia. Quarterback Ashton Daniels rushed for136 yards and five touchdowns for a team that's slightly better execution away against SMU from having a single blemish on the resume at Alabama. Norvell's team continues to fight, which is what you want to see from a squad under pressure to succeed.
Myrtle BeachProjection: Jacksonville State vs. OhioPotato Projection: North Dakota State vs. Western MichiganPuerto Rico Projection: Washington State vs. ToledoCure Projection: Cincinnati vs. Georgia StateIndependence Projection: Tulane vs. Oklahoma StateNew OrleansProjection: Troy vs. Liberty Armed Forces Projection: West Virginia vs. UConnPoinsettia Projection: Arizona State vs. New MexicoFrisco BowlProjection: Fresno State vs. North TexasThe Mean Green opened conference play Thursday night with a thrilling 45-44 win at Tulsa behind five total touchdowns from UCF transfer Tayven Jackson at quarterback. Baylor Hayes tallied five touchdowns, too, for the Golden Hurricane, but it wasn't enough after North Texas stopped Tulsa short in overtime on a two-point conversion try. North Texas won't play a ranked team the rest of the way, with the Nov. 21 showdown at Tulane potentially being for a spot in the American title game.New Mexico Projection: UNLV vs. LouisianaHawaiiProjection: Air Force vs. ECUPinstripeProjection: Virginia vs. Penn StateOne of the "wish we weren't here" games of the postseason, the Cavaliers and Nittany Lions each had playoff aspirations before recent meltdowns all but cratered those hopes. The light at the end of the tunnel for both teams is awfully dim after road blowouts in Week 5 were indictments of what's going wrong in recent weeks.Fenway Projection: North Carolina vs. MemphisIt's not going to be easy for the Tar Heels given their remaining schedule, but a respectable 37-26 rain-soaked loss to Notre Dame should give Bill Belichick's team a sense of confidence pushing forward. North Carolina is a red zone stop from being 3-1 with a brand-new roster and offense under Bobby Petrino.
MayoProjection: Duke vs. WisconsinThese teams are a combined 8-1 this season and both have hopes of getting to their respective conference championship games with a few breaks over the next two months. Wisconsin doesn't have to play Ohio State, Indiana or Oregon in the regular season, while the unbeaten Blue Devils go to Miami on Nov. 14 in what should be a season-defining showdown.68 Ventures Projection: Miami (Ohio) vs. Appalachian StateCactus Projection: Nebraska vs. Kansas StateMilitaryProjection: Army vs. LouisvilleBirminghamProjection: NC State vs. AuburnPop-TartsProjection: Clemson vs. HoustonThat was too close for comfort from the Cougars. Trailing 17-0 midway through the third quarter at home against UCF, Willie Fritz's team ran off 27 unanswered points to push to 4-1 overall and keep pace near the top of the Big 12. We're projecting the Big 12's runner-up or third-place team to play in Orlando against one of the ACC's best.AlamoProjection: UCLA vs. BYUGator Projection: Pittsburgh vs. Mississippi StateFriday night's win at Virginia Tech came with a price for the Panthers — starting quarterback Mason Heintschel, who went down with a leg injury during the first half — is out for the rest of the season. That's a significant development that could torch this rocket-fast start for Pat Narduzzi's team unless the unproven Holden Geriner can deliver.
The Bulldogs are unbeaten no more after Saturday's loss to Alabama, a mistake-filled performance that included a couple of throws from Kamario Taylor that he'd like to have back. Mississippi State plays LSU, Oklahoma and Texas over its next three games, so more season-defining moments are coming.Music CityProjection: Michigan vs. Missouri A frustrating first season for Kyle Whittingham is continuing at Michigan. After Bryce Underwood's two-interception outing during a loss at Minnesota, the Wolverines' coach said his staff would consider all angles during their bye week to try and fix this offense. Michigan (3-2) is lucky to not be 1-4 right now following consecutive losses to open Big Ten play.Who saw that performance coming out of 25th-ranked Missouri? The Tigers annihilated Florida, the first win over a top-10 team in Eli Drinkwitz's tenure, and in convincing fashion. Jamal Roberts eclipsed 200 yards on the ground, Austin Simmons had another 300-yard passing performance, and Missouri executed flawlessly to rebound from last week's loss at Mississippi State.
ReliaQuest Projection: Northwestern vs. Texas A&MThere's a realistic chance the Wildcats get to eight (or more) wins this season, which would mark another step forward for David Braun at Northwestern. Friday night's dominant victory over Penn State was a tone-setter, and a narrow setback at Indiana showed this team was going to be a tough out in the Big Ten.This would mark Texas A&M's first trip to Tampa in program history. The Aggies have never played in Orlando either, but we expect the Citrus Bowl to go after the highest-ranked SEC team not in the CFP.Sun Projection: Virginia Tech vs. ArizonaLas VegasProjection: Washington vs. OklahomaTexasProjection: Tennessee vs. Texas TechThe Vols' offense looked broken in Week 5 against Auburn before George MacIntyre came off the bench and gave Tennessee new life. He should be the starter for next week's trip to Arkansas as the Vols look to hang around the top-15 with a road victory.
CitrusProjection: Ole Miss vs. IowaFor now, we're picking the Rebels to finish as the second SEC team with nine wins but falling just short of a playoff bid despite a head-to-head loss with LSU in Week 2. Part of that has to do with the blowout loss at Florida, which is losing some of its luster after the Gators' setback at Missouri on Saturday. Both teams have challenging slates left, and it may come down to how each team performs against top-ranked Texas, a common opponent.For the Hawkeyes, their first loss of the season came at the hands of Ohio State. An 11-win campaign is still very much a possibility given the rest of the schedule, the most favorable in the Big Ten the rest of the way.First ResponderProjection: UTSA vs. SMULibertyProjection: UCF vs. KentuckyArizona Projection: UMass vs. WyomingHolidayProjection: USC vs. Wake ForestTen wins and a trip to California for bowl season? That's a possible — if not, probable — scenario unfolding for the Demon Deacons under second-year coach Jake Dickert. The only matchup left against a nationally-ranked opponent is SMU after splitting show-me matchups with Miami and Louisville last month.
College Football Playoff First roundProjection: (9) Oregon at (8) UtahTwo games to watch the rest of the way for the Utes in their quest to get to the Big 12 championship this season — and they all come in consecutive weeks against Houston, (at) Cincinnati and BYU during the second half of the slate. Trips to Arizona and TCU could be tricky in November, too. For now, Utah is our new projected conference champion out of what we're expecting to be a one-bid league.Projection: (10) Florida at (7) IndianaThe Gators were humbled at Missouri, but not selling all of my stock just yet on Florida after failing to show on the road. Jon Sumrall will need to fix some of this team's problems defensively, but the win over Ole Miss will age well, and there's still a clear path to 10 wins if the Gators can split upcoming matchups with Texas and Georgia. If that doesn't happen, welcome to the logjam that is 9-3 in the SEC.Projection: (11) LSU at (6) Notre DameLane Kiffin's team could punch that ticket with 10 victories, but they're going to need a hot finish and still have to play Alabama, Texas and Tennessee in November alone. We're tossing the Tigers back in this week and believe that, should Ole Miss and LSU each finish with nine wins, it will come down to overall resume and not the head-to-head meeting back in Week 3.
Projection: (12) JMU at (5) TexasIf the unbeaten Longhorns didn't have five remaining games against top-25 teams in conference play, we'd slot them inside the top four seed, but it's the toughest slate in the league over the second half of the campaign. There's bound to be a loss or two somewhere, which could be a blessing in disguise if it gets Texas out of the SEC Championship Game and another week of rest before the postseason.QuarterfinalsPeach  Projection: (9) Oregon vs. (1) MiamiSticking with our preseason top seed here, Miami will be No. 1 unless proven otherwise. This projection slots the Hurricanes as the 13-0 ACC champions. Any other record and seeding gets complicated for Mario Cristobal's squad.Cotton  Projection: (7) Indiana vs. (2) AlabamaPushing to No. 2 as the new projected SEC champion, Alabama has earned it. Russell's playing at an elite level in his first season as the Crimson Tide's starting quarterback, and we're starting to see a team that's gelling at the right time. Going into Starkville and responding with the biggest road margin over a ranked opponent in program history was telling.
Rose  Projection: (6) Notre Dame vs. (3) Ohio StateJeremiah Smith is the best player in the country, and Ohio State's defense might be figuring it out. After ranking 11th in the Big Ten in explosive plays allowed coming into Saturday's 31-14 win at Iowa, the Buckeyes settled down and kept chunk gains to a minimum. Notre Dame rolled in a rain-soaked Chapel Hill, but moves out of our top four this week due to a projected loss (to Miami in November) and a couple SEC teams with better overall strength of record.FiestaProjection: (5) Texas vs. (4) GeorgiaStrength of conference will matter greatly in a couple of months when the final playoff pairings are revealed. Five SEC teams could crack the top-12, and these are two of the best who could meet multiple times. Georgia hasn't gotten past the quarters since winning the second of its national championships under Kirby Smart, so that's a storyline to watch here.SemifinalsOrange  Projection: (4) Georgia vs. (1) MiamiSugar  Projection:  (7) Indiana vs. (3) Ohio State

title: Josh Huepel made the right call benching former 5-star Faizon Brandon -- now what? - CBS Sports
description: The Vols chose George MacIntyre's floor over Faizon Brandon's ceiling in a win over Auburn. Now they face a cross
body:
The Vols chose George MacIntyre's floor over Faizon Brandon's ceiling in a win over Auburn. Now they face a crossroads
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 3, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:07 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        With five minutes remaining in the first half against Auburn, Josh Heupel had a tough decision to make. The Tennessee coach chose to bench his five-star quarterback, and it proved to be the correct call as it sparked the Vols' offense to a 24-14 win over Auburn.Sophomore George MacIntyre took over for Faizon Brandon, and though he wasn't asked to do much, he was effective when called upon. MacIntyre completed 8 of 10 passing attempts for 86 yards, and one of those two incompletions was a drop on a perfect throw.That threat of the pass -- limited as it may have been -- opened up the ground game just enough for DeSean Bishop to run wild on the Auburn defense. Bishop exploded for 213 yards and a trio of touchdowns as the Vols averaged 5.0 yards per carry.The question now is, quite simply, what comes next?"We'll go watch the tape," Heupel said after the game. "Faizon ultimately didn't play his best football. The turnover on the sideline and some of the things, just progressions. I've said it a bunch to you guys. We're gonna need them both throughout the year."
In 2021, Heupel dealt with a similar scenario. Joe Milton won the starting job out of camp, but he was replaced by Hooker midway through the Vols' Week 2 game against Pittsburgh. Hooker took the job and ran with it, becoming one of Tennessee's best quarterbacks of the 21st century.Of course, there are a few key differences that don't apply here. The first is that Milton left the Pitt game after getting banged up, not necessarily due to his ineffectiveness -- although he did have some bad misses through the air.The biggest difference is that Hooker wasn't a player Heupel recruited to Tennessee, and he certainly wasn't a five-star freshman making big money.
Prior to his firing, Jeremy Pruitt landed Hooker on the transfer market, and Heupel's staff recruited Milton to Knoxville. There was no expectation that Hooker would be the future of the quarterback position for the Vols.Brandon, on the other hand, arrived with sky-high expectations. The No. 3 quarterback in the 2026 signing class, Brandon was hand-picked by the Vols coaching staff and still projects as a future star at Tennessee.Whether he can become a star this season is very much up in the air, and there's a case for Heupel to leave Brandon on the bench for the foreseeable future.
Brandon's low floor could cost VolsThrough the first three games of the season -- against Furman, Georgia Tech and Kennesaw State -- Brandon flashed some of the high ceiling that made him a blue-chip prospect. He made tough throws and used his legs to create plays that weren't there.However, against Texas and Auburn, we saw how low his floor could be. In almost six quarters of SEC action, Brandon has completed 52.6% of his passes for 145 yards, one touchdown and one interception.When Brandon was pulled against Auburn, he had zero passing yards and a pick. He was hesitant when dropping back to pass, and the interception resulted from Brandon staring down an open receiver until he wasn't open anymore.
With MacIntyre in the game, there was a noticeable improvement, even in limited action. The sophomore saw the field more clearly, and MacIntyre wasn't afraid to pull the trigger when there was an open window.The best throw of the day for MacIntyre was a 42-yard dart to Mike Matthews, which was the result of the sophomore letting a pass fly over the middle of the field. That big gain set up a 25-yard touchdown run from Bishop.Just the remote threat of a passing attack meant the Auburn defense couldn't tee off on Bishop and the Vols' run game, which is the bread and butter of Heupel's offense.
"George's ability to throw the football in the second half allowed us to create a big play, in particular the one to Mike early,' Heupel said. "In general, it allowed us to take advantage of some stuff they were giving us."Brandon's long-term ceiling is undeniable. He's a supremely talented football player, but his floor is so low that playing him could cost Tennessee in the more winnable games on its schedule.Tennessee can't waste its defenseFirst-year defensive coordinator Jim Knowles has already been a value add for Tennessee. When the Vols were sputtering on offense, the defense kept them in the game until Bishop got rolling.
Tennessee allowed just two touchdowns, and one of them can be laid at the feet of Brandon, who threw an interception at the Vols' 19-yard line. Auburn cashed in on that short field, but it was tough sledding for the rest of the game.Perhaps the play of Tennessee's defense will give Heupel more reason to roll with MacIntyre as the starter for a while.The defense has proven that it doesn't need much run support to win games. Tennessee had the ball with a chance to beat No. 1 Texas, even with a putrid offensive showing that resulted in 10 sacks.
On the season, Tennessee has yet to allow more than 24 points in a single game, and seven of those points were the result of a punt block against Georgia Tech. If MacIntyre can take care of the football and give the Vols something that resembles an average offense -- just as he did against Auburn -- the defense might be able to carry the load.

body:
The NFL is coming off one of its craziest weeks in recent memory, as Week 3 tied a league record for the number of one-score games. Judging by the Cleveland Browns upset win over the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday, Week 4 promises to continue the madness as we flip the calendar to October and close out the first month of the regular season. Of course, between work, daily chores, and craziness that is life, it's hard to keep pace with all that's happening across the NFL. For instance, you might not have realized that a massive trade popped up midweek, in which the Cowboys acquired standout corner Joey Porter Jr. from the Steelers. Or, from a scheduling standpoint, we have early morning football on Sunday, with the Commanders and Colts kicking off from London. So, as you get ready for another Sunday of full-fledged NFL action, we want you to be as informed as possible before you line up any wagers you may make. With that in mind, here's a look at some last-minute Week 4 picks, including five best bets.NFL odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook.  Los Angeles Rams at Philadelphia EaglesSunday, 1 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo, try for free)Both clubs enter Week 4 after rather demoralizing losses on the road. Case Keenum sliced Philly up on "Monday Night Football," and they now have to turn around and square off against the Matthew Stafford-led Rams on a short week. Meanwhile, L.A. lost a heartbreaker in Denver, which dropped the preseason "superteam" to 1-2 through the first three weeks. Each of these teams has yet to live up to their lofty expectations so far this year, but I think the Rams are in a better spot to pull off the win here, especially with the return of wideout Puka Nacua. 
At first glance, you might be eager to take the Eagles as a home dog, but they've historically not been kind to bettors in this setting. Since 2021 (Sirianni's first season as head coach), Philadelphia is 0-5 straight up (1-4 ATS) as a home underdog. When watching them this season, it's clear their offense is still a work in progress. The Eagles have yet to score in the first quarter this season (the only team in the NFL yet to score) and have the highest three-and-out rate (29%) since 2025. When you pair that with a defense that has yet to generate a turnover and has registered just three sacks, there's an opportunity for the Rams to get out to an early lead and never look back. As we saw on Monday night, when you get the Eagles into a pass-heavy game script, it's not exactly "The Greatest Show on Turf," and they'll try to win in Week 4 without top wideout DeVonta Smith (hamstring).  Projected score: Rams 26, Eagles 20The pick: Rams -3.5Green Bay Packers at Tampa Bay BuccaneersSunday, 1 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo, try for free)It's a make-or-break game for each of these NFC squads, but I'd argue it's most important for the Packers. Sure, the Bucs are teetering with a 0-3 record and just lost Baker Mayfield (thumb) for the next few weeks, but a loss here would be a straight-up embarrassment for Green Bay. I don't care if the offensive line has any many holes as a Cheesehead, if the Packers can't beat a Baker-less Bucs team that'll be quarterbacked by undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels, the entire operation needs to be in question. Jordan Love has struggled this season with the second-highest off-target rate (19.4%) and second-lowest completion percentage (52.4%) in the NFL. However, he's also been under siege quite a bit, facing the third-highest amount of pressure (44.7%). The offensive line for the Packers is still a massive question, but Love might get a little more time in the pocket this week with the Bucs logging the second-lowest pressure rate (28.3%) in the league. Tampa Bay is also on a 12-game coverless streak, which is the longest ATS losing streak since 1970. 
Projected score: Packers 27, Buccaneers 20The pick: Packers -3.5Dallas Cowboys at Houston TexansSunday, 1 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo, try for free)The Texans are 0-3 for the second year in a row, and I don't believe they'll resurrect themselves as they did in 2025. Houston's offensive line remains a monumental weakness, and it's affecting all facets of the offense. In pass protection, they're allowing the third-most pressures (52) and are tied for the second-most sacks (10) allowed. On the ground, the Texans average just 3.6 yards per carry, which is tied for the fifth-lowest in the NFL. Their 2.15 yards after contact per rush are the second-lowest.So, while the Cowboys' defense has remained abysmal, they might actually find some success against the Texans' defense. That's particularly true if Dallas' offense continues to put points on the board. This season, the Cowboys have the highest drive-scoring rate (61.5%) in the league. If Dak Prescott and company build up a lead, C.J. Stroud will be forced to pass and test newly acquired corner Joey Porter Jr., who appears set to make his debut following this week's trade. Meanwhile, I also wonder how much of a home-field advantage Reliant Stadium will be and how many Dallas fans will make the trip to Houston/already be in the area. 
Projected score: Cowboys 27, Texans 23The pick: Cowboys +3Los Angeles Chargers at Seattle SeahawksSunday, 4:25 p.m. (CBS, Stream on Paramount+)We're going back to the well and laying a touchdown with the Seahawks against an inferior team. It burned us last week against Marcus Mariota and the Commanders, but it doesn't change the logic. Seattle is arguably the best team in the NFL, and they just got their Super Bowl-winning quarterback back. Sure, he threw two interceptions (including a pick-six), but Sam Darnold also completed 31 of 45 for 379 yards and four passing touchdowns. At home, I think we get a much cleaner and more prolific showing from him. Even if he does turn it over again, these Chargers have shown us that they can still lose despite winning the turnover battle. They are +4 over the Bills in turnover margin and still found a way to lose. Los Angeles looks absolutely lost as an organization, especially on offense where they are averaging 14.7 points per game (fourth-fewest in the NFL). I don't expect the unit to suddenly revive itself against a Mike Macdonald-led defense that is allowing the third-fewest points per game (16.7) and fewest total yards per game (228.7). Projected score: Seahawks 33, Chargers 20The pick: Seahawks -7Miami Dolphins at Minnesota VikingsSunday, 4:05 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo, try for free)To put it delicately, it's been a rough go of it for the Dolphins. We knew they weren't going to be competitive this season, but after watching them through the first three weeks, it stands to reason they won't even win a game in 2026. To make matters worse, they just lost star running back De'Von Achane, their most prolific offensive player. 
Now, a bad offense gets even worse and faces Brian Flores' defense. Flores, who currently serves as Minnesota's defensive coordinator, was the head coach of the Dolphins for three seasons (2019-2021) before being fired. Surely, he'd like to stick it to his former team and will do so by continuing to blitz the quarterback. The Vikings have the highest blitz rate (71%) in the NFL. That'll be quite the mismatch for a Miami team that is tied for the third-most sacks allowed (9). Sure, Minnesota won't have No.1 receiver Justin Jefferson (ankle) for this game, but it might not matter with Flores pulling the levers on defense. The overall trends look favorable for a Vikings win/cover as well. Miami is 0-3 ATS this season and was a double-digit underdog in all of those prior contests. Meanwhile, Minnesota is 8-0 straight-up and 7-1 ATS over its last eight games. title: Florida's reality check: Mizzou exposes flaws that could derail Gators' SEC hopes - CBS Sports
description: Missouri certainly revealed a few weaknesses on Saturday, but is it time to hit the panic button?
body:
Missouri certainly revealed a few weaknesses on Saturday, but is it time to hit the panic button?
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 3, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:43 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The No. 8 Florida Gators entered Week 5 as one of the hottest teams in all of college football. With a statement win against Ole Miss under their belt and an offense that was averaging 53.5 points per game through the first month of the season, it was fair to suggest that Jon Sumrall had already re-established a proud Florida program to its desired status of SEC title contender. With challenges left against Texas and Georgia, the job was far from done, but prior to Saturday, the belief around Gainesville was that this team could play with and score on almost anyone. That context made Saturday's 45-17 loss at No. 25 Missouri not just a massive shock to those singing the praises of Sumrall and Florida's resurgence, but also a devastating reality check on this team's strengths and weaknesses against conference competition. "We did not play to our standard," Sumrall said after the game. "Embarrassing performance in every phase. It starts with the coaching, it starts with me. I just told the guys in the locker room right now I expect everyone to be a man which means be accountable for your actions and own it. I'm going to start that way right now. I'm not going to point fingers at anybody, but we have to play a lot better. 
"I'm sick to my freaking stomach with what we just did." 
        
            
                College football winners, losers in Week 5: Keelon Russell sparks Alabama to new level, Florida collapses
                
                    Shehan Jeyarajah                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
How Missouri neutralized Florida's offense Florida's superpower, it seemed, was the offense and the rushing attack helmed by Jaden Baugh. With 600 yards and 11 touchdowns in the first four games, Baugh was becoming a key figure in the Heisman Trophy race, and his electric running style was perfectly matched with the creative ways that offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner aligns the offense. It could be blocked well or schemed up, but if Baugh could just get a little bit of space, he has the explosive ability to break a game wide open. Unfortunately, that space was hard to find against Missouri's defensive front, exposing real concerns about whether this is one of the best offenses in the country. The Tigers pushed Florida's front off the ball and filled running lanes, holding Baugh to just 13 total rushing yards on 12 attempts. As a team, Florida was limited to 42 rushing yards on 25 attempts and had no runs of 20+ yards after totaling 10 such runs (most in the SEC) through the first four games. With struggles to run the football, Florida was left putting a lot more weight on quarterback Aaron Philo to make tough plays against a Missouri defense that could tee off on obvious passing downs. Philo was sacked three times and struggled to open things up with deep passing, leaving the offense to short completions and the hope that the Gators' skill could win in the open field. Philo finished completing 21-of-34 passes for 192 yards and one touchdown with no interceptions, but he was replaced by backup quarterback Tramell Jones in the fourth quarter and watched Florida's only second-half touchdown from the sideline.
Philo and the passing attack were not the most productive pieces of Florida's offense in the wins against Auburn and Ole Miss. The transfer from Georgia Tech threw for 204 yards against Auburn and then 196 against Ole Miss, but those numbers raised no alarm when the team was scoring 40+ points every time it took the field. The passing attack was shorthanded, still missing starting wide receiver Vernell Brown III with an injury, but if Florida was going to be judged as a true SEC title contender, it needed to be more than a one-trick pony on offense. Not just an offensive problem Arguably as alarming as Florida's inability to run the ball was the way that Missouri's offense gashed the Gators for big plays, especially in the second half. The Tigers' front did a great job moving defenders to create clear running lanes for Jamal Roberts, who put together a career day with 211 rushing yards and three rushing touchdowns. From physicality to run fits to open-field tackling, there wasn't much that graded out well for Florida on defense, and it reframes how the Gators will have to win if they are going to remain in the hunt for an SEC title. Austin Simmons had a field day picking apart the Gators secondary, too, completing 23-of-30 passes for 340 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions. Missouri wideouts were finding their way behind defenders and, like the run game, exposing a troubling tackling effort from Florida in the open field. 
It's worth noting that safety Bryce Thornton was ruled out for the game due to an injury, but if his absence leads to this kind of success, then the depth of Florida's pass defense should absolutely be a concern when graded against the standard of the SEC's best.  How Florida moves forward Now, if this reality check feels like a cold shower for Florida's hot start, it's important to warm up to the idea that things might not be as bad as they looked on the field in Columbia. Winning on the road in the SEC is hard, and this program is now 1-7 in its past eight conference road games. It's also hard to maintain momentum after running so hot with back-to-back emotional wins against Auburn and Ole Miss. Jon Sumrall was very aware that the success could be intoxicating and warned that if his team did not take a humble approach to their preparation, they would get humbled on the field. "Here's the deal, and I told the team this, you have to humble yourself or you will be humbled," Sumrall said on Monday. "If we don't look in the mirror and own where we are deficient still, someone will show it to us."  
That's exactly what happened on Saturday in Columbia as Missouri put Florida's deficiencies on full display for the rest of the SEC and the country to observe. Florida still has one of the best running backs in the country and one of the most dangerous offensive attacks, but the counter-punch, if a team can stop the run, does not appear fully formed. Defensively, this is a group that has playmakers but also gives up 37.3 points per game in conference play. These facts are important when we're evaluating Florida's spot among the top teams in the SEC. Because if the Gators are getting pushed around in the trenches against Missouri, what will be the expectation, then, when they face the likes of Texas and Georgia later in the season? Those defenses must be thrilled to know that shutting down Florida's ground game can have such a wide-ranging impact on their success.To Sumrall's credit, he has offered regular reminders to Florida fans that this team is not perfect and still a work in progress. He has embraced the excitement and attitude that come with Florida when it's buzzing with swagger, but now has evidence for his team that they are not good enough to overcome bad performances. It's normal for a team to have a bad day on the road, but true contenders are able to find ways to punch back. Outside of a late touchdown drive in the final minute from the backup quarterback, the Gators did not offer much in terms of a response to Missouri's second-half success. The Tigers took control of the game in the middle eight (17-0), and it slipped away from the Gators, possession by possession. 
Florida is still a team with the talent and explosiveness to beat anyone on its schedule, including Texas and Georgia. But what Saturday's loss laid bare was that this year's team lacks the roster depth or the consistency in performance to be compared with some of the most successful Florida teams of the 21st Century, even if the Gators' stats and rankings suggested otherwise.Florida is still an SEC title contender and very much in the mix for the College Football Playoff thanks to its win against Ole Miss, but if the Gators are going to finish the season competing with the best teams in the country, they cannot afford the kind of mistakes on display Saturday. Florida plays at Texas on Oct. 17 after a game against South Carolina, then faces Georgia in their rivalry game on Oct. 31. One of those games will likely need to be a Florida win, and achieving that will require a lot of work and humility over the next week.

schema.headline: Florida's reality check: Mizzou exposes flaws that could derail Gators' SEC hopes - CBS Sports

The Week 4 clash pits two high-flying offenses against defenses that struggled to stop anyone through their first three games. Bryce Young is turning into a standout quarterback in real time, and the Lions feature the best wide receiver-running back tandem in the NFL with Jahmyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown. Points ought not to be hard to come by in this primetime battle.Detroit scored exactly 31 points in all of its games thus far and came away with a pair of victories. The Panthers were off to a similarly prolific start but hit an unforeseen road block a week ago with their 21-18 loss at the Cleveland Browns. This is a difficult spot to find a bounce back, but Dave Canales' team upset two playoff teams a year ago and are built to hang with the league's third-highest-scoring squad.With a win, the Lions would remain within close striking distance of the NFC North lead. The Panthers need a victory to avoid falling into a 1-3 hole and slipping behind in an NFC South that should be up for grabs until season's end.Where to watch Panthers vs. Lions liveDate: Sunday, Oct. 4 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ETLocation: Bank of America Stadium (Charlotte, N.C.)TV: NBC | Streaming: Fubo (try for free)Follow: CBS Sports AppOdds: Lions -3.5, O/U 51.5 via DraftKings SportsbookKey storylinesPanthers thin at cornerback: The Panthers opened the year with an elite cornerback tandem but lost both starters to injuries in Week 3. Carolina placed Jaycee Horn (quad) and Mike Jackson (groin) on injured reserve following the loss to the Cleveland Browns, and not only will they miss at least four games, but Horn could be done for the year with his torn muscle. There is no ideal time to insert two backups into the lineup, but this week against a high-octane offense is about the worst situation imaginable. Chau Smith-Wade, Akayleb Evans and rookie Will Lee III are the only available cornerbacks on the roster.Shootout potential: In addition to the Panthers' potential woes in the back end of their defense, the Lions have been unable to contain each of their three opponents this year and are in for another challenge to close out the first month of the season. Detroit ranks last in points allowed and is just 2 yards back of last place in yardage, too. Two subpar defenses and two prolific offenses square off in this contest, which makes Sunday night ripe for a high-scoring affair.Bryce Young's breakout: Hardly anyone saw it coming, but Bryce Young is the NFL's leading passer through three games. Perhaps his tremendous start should not come as too much of a surprise considering he finally found his footing last year under coach Dave Canales, but it is an eyebrow-raising development nonetheless. The former No. 1 overall pick appears more comfortable than at any point in what, until late last year, was a disappointing start to his career. He could have a field day against a Lions defense that ranks last against the pass.Jared Goff in rare air: Only six quarterbacks in NFL history opened a season with 800 passing yards, eight touchdowns, zero interceptions and a 70% completion rate across the first three games. Jared Goff is in that group, which also includes Kirk Cousins, Patrick Mahomes, Drew Brees, Tom Brady and Peyton Manning. That is not bad company. Goff is also one of just three signal-callers this year to start all three games and remain clean in the interception department. Combine that terrific play through the air with Jahmyr Gibbs' electric rushing production, and this Detroit offense is as well-rounded as they come.Welcome to primetime: Carolina faces the longest active "Sunday Night Football" drought in the NFL but will finally snap a 10-year absence when it hosts Detroit. The last time the Panthers played on Sunday night was in 2016 when they dropped a 40-7 clunker to the Seattle Seahawks. Their return to playoff caliber earned them three primetime appearances this season, which is their most in a single year since that 2016 campaign which resulted in a trip to the Super Bowl.PredictionCarolina will have no answers for Amon-Ra St. Brown without its top two cornerbacks, and Jahmyr Gibbs has never seen a defense he cannot torch. And on the other side of the ball, the Lions own a beleaguered secondary of their own, and there is no reason to believe the league's worst pass defense will keep Bryce Young in check — especially if wide receiver Jalen Coker returns to the lineup. The Panthers posted 37 points in their Week 1 home shootout with the Chicago Bears and could outdo that number against an even leakier defense. In a game where one stop might be the difference, the home team holds the edge.
Pick: Panthers 38, Lions 34

        The final numbered UFC event of 2026 has a pair of headliners set, and some of the promotion's most familiar names will be in action at UFC 335 on Dec. 12 in Las Vegas. In the main event, Charles Oliveira will put the ceremonial BMF championship on the line against Diego Lopes, while former middleweight and two-time light heavyweight champion Alex Pereira will face Sergei Pavlovich in heavyweight action. The pair of fights were announced on Saturday during the UFC 332 broadcast.Oliveira is coming off a dominant BMF title win over Max Holloway at UFC 326 in March. Some fans felt that Oliveira's win was not in the spirit of the BMF belt, as he used takedowns and ground control to completely neutralize Holloway's vaunted striking game. That said, Oliveira has one of the deepest histories of true "BMF action," having set the record for most UFC wins by submission (17), by finish (21), and most post-fight bonuses (14).A former lightweight champion, Oliveira transitioned from a solid part of the roster to one of the elite fighters in one of the deepest divisions in the sport.In Lopes, Oliveira faces a fighter who, since losing his Octagon debut, has steadily climbed the featherweight ranks. While Lopes has proven a force at 145 pounds, he has twice come up short in opportunities to become champion, losing twice to Alexander Volkanovski in title fights.
UFC 335 will mark Lopes' lightweight debut.Pereira came up short in a historic bid to become a three-division UFC champion at UFC Freedom 250 when he was stopped by Ciryl Gane in a fight for the interim heavyweight title. Prior to that fight, Pereira vacated the light heavyweight belt in the middle of his second reign as champ.Pereira had won middleweight gold by knocking out old kickboxing rival Israel Adesanya before losing the belt back in the rematch. He then moved to light heavyweight where he became a dominant champion outside of a decision loss to Magomed Ankalaev. Pereira avenged the Ankalaev loss and regained his title in their immediate rematch, taking just 80 seconds to score a stoppage.
Pavlovich has become a mainstay of the heavyweight rankings, compiling a 9-3 UFC record. Those three losses came to top heavyweight fighters Alistair Overeem, Tom Aspinall (for the interim heavyweight title) and Alexander Volkov.

body:
Russell sparks the Crimson Tide in a blowout road win, while the Gators collapse against Missouri and Bryce Underwood struggles in Michigan's upset loss

        Mississippi State's matchup against Alabama was billed as one of the best quarterback battles of the season. Instead, it proved to be a coming-out party for Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell, who emerged as one of the biggest winners of Week 5. The sophomore outdueled Kamario Taylor to deliver the Tide a fifth straight dominant victory. Several other AP Top 25 teams were challenged, including big deficits by No. 20 Houston. Outside of No. 8 Florida, all of them eventually managed to pull through. There are plenty more matchups to keep an eye on as we head into primetime. Four ranked teams play road games, including No. 4 Miami traveling to Clemson. A few other teams in the late-night slate can make statements, including Baylor-Arizona State and Cincinnati-Arizona. Here are the biggest winners and losers of Week 5 before the evening slate. Winner: AlabamaBeware, college football: the Alabama death machine is back. The Crimson Tide went on the road against a nationally-ranked Mississippi State and delivered kill shot after kill shot to Kamario Taylor and the Bulldogs. The Bulldogs turned the ball over four times, including two from Taylor on the first two drives, to set up a blowout victory. 
But the story of the day was under center, where Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell was sensational. The sophomore threw for 285 yards and three touchdowns while adding another score on the ground. With Russell under center, Alabama's offense is starting to look like the unstoppable Michael Penix Jr. unit DeBoer fielded at Washington. There's a lot of football left, but the Tide look like a serious national championship contender. Loser: FloridaThe Gators got plenty of love after crushing Ole Miss, including a rise into the AP top 10 for the first time since 2021. That trip won't last long after the Gators completely collapsed against No. 25 Missouri in a stunning 45-17 decision. The Tigers completely dominated the trenches, holding Jadan Baugh to only 13 yards rushing. Florida rose to the top of the SEC and playoff conversation after a hot start, but much of it is now in doubt after the emotional swing. Now, the Gators will wonder what could have been as they face No. 1 Texas and No. 2 Georgia in the coming weeks. 
Winner: WisconsinThe Badgers haven't had much to celebrate during the Luke Fickell era, but a 31-3 decimation of Pat Fitzgerald's Michigan State felt like a deep exhale. Wisconsin jumped out to a 17-0 lead and got more than 140 yards passing and rushing from quarterback Colton Joseph. Wisconsin's administration gambled they could get more out of the Fickell hire with additional roster investment. Since a slow start against Notre Dame, the Badgers have looked the part, rattling off four straight victories. A road trip against No. 23 UCLA will reveal the mettle of this team, but they're playing with tremendous confidence. Loser: Penn StateWhen Penn State fired James Franklin, the hope was that the Nittany Lions could find a coach able to punch up and beat the elite teams in college football. Through two games, Matt Campbell has proven unable to take care of business against the middle class. 
One week after collapsing against Wisconsin, Penn State went on the road and got destroyed 34-13 against Northwestern. The Nittany Lions were obliterated in the trenches specifically, losing the rushing battle by an astonishing 413-48. Penn State is at serious risk of missing a bowl game. Campbell's contract is fully guaranteed, but he couldn't have drawn up a worse start to his career. Winner: RB Aiden Flora, Iowa StateThe Cyclones didn't return a single starter from their 2025 team (as many followed Campbell to State College). But five games into the season, one of the few players who stayed looks like the top breakout player in the Big 12. Flora carried the ball only 15 times in two seasons under Campbell. First-year coach Jimmy Rogers had a better plan. Flora exploded for 212 yards rushing and three touchdowns in a dramatic 45-42 win against West Virginia. Amazingly, he also added 48 yards passing and two touchdowns through the air as offensive coordinator Tyler Roehl found perfect ways to use him. 
Iowa State is up to 3-2 after stunning the Mountaineers and has played exceptionally well in all five games. Rogers' rebuild is well ahead of schedule. 
Loser: QB Bryce Underwood, MichiganMichigan's offense has lost its magic. While quarterback Bryce Underwood is an easy target, the sophomore was a total disaster in a 20-14 loss against Minnesota. Underwood completed only 10 of 21 passes for 101 yards and two interceptions in the loss as Michigan started 0-2 in Big Ten play for the first time since 2014. Underwood is completing only 54.5% of his passes with two touchdowns and three interceptions against power conference competition. The Wolverines will seriously consider a change during the bye week. 
Winner: WR Jeremiah Smith, Ohio StateWe've had Smith as a winner essentially every week of the year, but what do you want us to do? In Week 5, Smith passed Emeka Egbuka and Chris Olave, respectively, to set the Ohio State records for receptions and receiving touchdowns. After recording 11 catches for 206 yards and two touchdowns against Iowa, Smith is up to 44 catches for 823 yards and nine touchdowns. The season isn't even halfway over! Loser: CaliforniaTosh Lupoi seemed to be an exciting hire to maximize quarterback Jaren-Keawe Sagapolutele, but he's lost every ounce of goodwill after a miserable 2-3 start to the season. The Golden Bears lost an awful game 39-31 against UNLV on Saturday after going down 24-7 at halftime. Sagapolutele left the loss against UNLV with an apparent head injury, though backup Jackson Brousseau played well in his absence. Still, Lupoi will have to consider all options on offense to right the ship. As it stands, the Golden Bears will be heavy underdogs in every game until rival Stanford on Nov. 21. 
Winner: QB Dante Reno, YaleOne day after losing his father, Yale quarterback Dante Reno stepped up with a masterful performance. The junior shook off an early pick-six to respond with 298 yards and four touchdowns as the Bulldogs outlasted Merrimack 41-24 on Saturday. Dante's father, Tony Reno, coached at Yale from 2012-25, winning five Ivy League titles and ranking No. 2 on the program's all-time wins list. He was forced to step down due to health issues before his untimely passing on Friday. Tony was 52.

title: Ohio State's Jeremiah Smith breaks Buckeyes' all-time WR records vs. Iowa - CBS Sports
description: The junior wideout needed only 34 career games to pass Chr
body:
The junior wideout needed only 34 career games to pass Chris Olave for touchdowns and Emeka Egbuka, whom he also passed for career receptions on Saturday

        Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith just recorded his 36th career touchdown to become the all-time leader in program history. Smith separated for a 57-yard touchdown reception in the Buckeyes' 31-14 win over No. 14 Iowa -- his second of the day -- to set the record. After the catch, Smith celebrated by hitting the Heisman Trophy pose. Smith passed former All-Big Ten receiver Chris Olave (35) to reach the mark, also passing David Boston in the process. Olave needed 47 career games to tie the record. Smith is playing in his 34th game, only halfway through his third season of eligibility. A few minutes later, Smith also broke Emeka Egbuka's record of 205 career receptions. Smith became the second player in Big Ten history to post 200-yard performances in consecutive games, joining Indiana's Ty Fryfogle. Smith caught 11 passes for 206 yards and two touchdowns in the victory. He also joined Jaxon Smith-Njigba as the only Ohio State players to record multiple 200-yard games in their careers. 
The junior from Florida was rated the No. 1 player in his recruiting class and was regarded as one of the best wide receiver recruits in college football history. Somehow, he's exceeded every expectation. Smith led Ohio State to the national championship in 2024 with a transcendent run in the College Football Playoff. He followed it up with a conference-leading 87 catches in 2025. However, his junior season is already blowing the rest out of the water as Smith has recorded at least 150 yards and a touchdown in four of his five appearances this season. 
Now, Smith is up to 207 catches for 3,371 yards and 36 touchdowns, all Ohio State records. That puts him only 237 yards away from John Standeford's Big Ten receiving record and three touchdowns away from Braylon Edwards' mark at Michigan. The receptions mark is likely out of play, though, as Joe Tiller's offenses at Purdue produced 300-reception receiver Taylor Stubblefield from 2001-04.

title: Where Jeremiah Smith ranks among the greatest college receivers of the 21st century - CBS Sports
description: Jeremiah Smith posted his second consecutive 200-plus yard performance on Saturday afternoon against Iowa to help lead Ohio State to a 3
body:
Jeremiah Smith posted his second consecutive 200-plus yard performance on Saturday afternoon against Iowa to help lead Ohio State to a 31-14 road win. But where does he rank among the all-time greats?What separates the legends is the ability to produce even when the other team knows you are going to get the football. In his first two years, you could argue that Smith benefited from being part of an elite receiving corps that forced opponents to pick their poison. This year, he is the engine and is carrying the offense through five games. Smith has 44 catches for 823 receiving yards and nine touchdowns through five games. The next-best receiver for Ohio State has been Devin McCuin, with 17 catches for 245 yards and two touchdowns. Every defense knows that Julian Sayin wants to throw the ball to No. 4, and no one -- even stout defenses like Texas and Iowa -- has been able to force Sayin to look anywhere else. That's the kind of dominance reserved for the game's hyper elite, and it puts Smith in rare air among the best receivers college football has seen in recent memory. 
We put together our top 10 receivers of the last 26 years in college football, where productivity matters, but there is a considerable amount of eye-test involved. The 10 best wide receivers of the 21st century
                            
    
                                                
                    
    1. Larry FitzgeraldThe people's Heisman winner in 2003, Larry Fitzgerald, was one of the most stunning combinations of size, speed, hands and body control the game's ever seen. His Hall-of-Fame NFL career is what most fans remember now, but in college Fitzgerald was doing outrageous things on a near-weekly basis at Pittsburgh -- which wasn't exactly a dominant football team. Every game, every opponent knew the ball was going to go to No. 1, and it didn't matter one bit. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    2. Calvin JohnsonNo one on this list played in a less receiver-friendly situation than Johnson, but one could argue that it only grew his legend. Johnson was dominant from the moment he stepped onto the field in Atlanta. He did that in spite of playing in what was a run-heavy offense with a quarterback who never completed more than 50% of his passes in Johnson's three years, but the inaccuracy from the quarterback position also helped Johnson show off his insane catch radius and athleticism that made Megatron an all-time great at the NFL level as well. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    3. Jeremiah SmithIf he continues on the pace he's on the rest of this season, he's going to have a strong argument for this list's top spot. What makes Smith stand out is his dominance from the moment he set foot on campus at Ohio State. Despite coming into a stacked receiver room with future NFL talent, Smith topped 1,000 yards as a freshman and has only improved since then. If he can maintain the outrageous pace he's on now (or even come close to it), he can absolutely climb to the very top of this list. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    4. DeVonta SmithThe only receiver to win the Heisman Trophy this century, Smith's 2020 campaign at Alabama was an all-timer. His 117 catches, 1,856 yards and 23 touchdowns all led the nation in one of the best receiving seasons in history. Smith's slight frame raised questions at the pro level (which he's answered emphatically in Philly), but in college, he was uncoverable in his final two seasons at Alabama and belongs near the top of any list. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    5. Justin BlackmonBlackmon's NFL career has made many people forget how dominant he was at Oklahoma State. In his sophomore and junior seasons, he combined for 233 catches, 3,304 yards and 38 touchdowns, winning back-to-back Biletnikoff awards and All-America honors. Even understanding he was playing in a pass-heavy offense, those were preposterous numbers, and he more than looked the part with his physical attributes. 
That didn't translate at the NFL level for whatever reason, but Blackmon deserves to be remembered as one of the best we've seen at the collegiate level. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    6. Charles Rogers Another NFL bust and a tragic off-field story, Rogers' time at Michigan State was nothing short of incredible. He was not playing on particularly good Spartans squads in his two years of actually playing in East Lansing, but he was a physically dominant receiver with tremendous size, speed and leaping ability. 
Over two years in the early 2000s, Rogers piled up 2,551 yards and 25 touchdowns on just 125 catches, making the most of limited opportunities to earn the No. 2 overall pick in the 2003 NFL Draft. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    7. Michael CrabtreeCrabtree's freshman season is one of the all-time greats in college football history, with 134 catches for 1,962 yards and 22 touchdowns. He played in an offense that was tailored to huge productivity under Mike Leach at Texas Tech, but he was undeniably a freak and absolutely tortured Big 12 defenses for his two years in Lubbock. Crabtree racked up a pair of All-American nods, two Biletnikoff awards and a fifth-place Heisman finish as a sophomore -- ironically, his least productive of his two seasons in college.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    8. Braylon EdwardsMichigan has not often been known as a high-flying passing attack, but when Edwards was in Ann Arbor, the Wolverines had one of the nation's elite pass catchers. Edwards put together three seasons with over 1,000 yards and more than 10 touchdowns over his career with the Wolverines. What's incredible is going back and watching Edwards's highlights, where the Wolverines are regularly in 22 personnel with Edwards as the lone receiver split out wide, and he was still able to produce consistently, even as the only possible deep-ball threat on the field. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    9. Ja'Marr ChaseChase really only had one season of elite-level play in college football, but what a season it was. He racked up 84 catches for 1,780 yards and 20 touchdowns as part of LSU's all-time great offense in the Tigers' 2019 national championship-winning season. The Tigers have had their share of elite receivers, but none dominated the college ranks at the same level as Chase. You know someone was a special talent when they could effectively put up one huge year, opt out of the next season and still get drafted No. 5 overall.  

                            
    
                                                
                    
    10. Amari CooperCooper had a 1,000-yard season as a freshman on Alabama's 2012 national title team and as a junior put up more than 1,700 yards and 16 touchdowns in a season that earned him third-place in Heisman Trophy voting. Like a handful of others on this list, Cooper didn't quite live up to the billing as a superstar in the NFL, but at the collegiate level, he was a monster for the Tide. Honorable mentionJulio Jones, A.J. Green, Andre Johnson, Sammy Watkins, Malik Nabers, Roy Williams, Travis Hunter
I'll be honest, I do not feel good about having a list without Julio Jones, A.J. Green or Andre Johnson, but I also struggled to take anyone off of the list. As it turns out, there have been a lot more than just 10 great wide receivers over the past 26 years in college football. Jones was obviously a freak but the productivity at Alabama wasn't quite at the level of those in the top 10 -- Jones was never an All-American, which shocked me going back through profiles. The same caveat applies to Green and Johnson, and all three went on to dominant professional careers.

title: Pitt QB Mason Heintschel suffers season-ending knee injury amid 5-0 start - CBS Sports
description: Heintschel went down during the Panthers' win over Virginia Tech on Friday night
body:
Heintschel went down during the Panthers' win over Virginia Tech on Friday night
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 3, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:03 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        After the elation of their 35-33 victory on the road over Virginia Tech on Friday night, Pittsburgh received some unfortunate news on Saturday when testing revealed starting quarterback Mason Heintschel suffered a season-ending knee injury, sources told CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz. An MRI revealed Heintschel suffered an ACL tear, sources said, and the 5-0 Panthers will now have to continue their season in pursuit of an ACC Championship without their starting quarterback. Heintschel leads the nation in touchdown passes with 14 this season, completing 66.2% of his passes for 1,304 yards and just one interception prior to suffering his injury on Friday night in Lane Stadium. In Heintschel's place, Holden Greiner stepped in and performed well for the Panthers. Greiner went 8-for-12 for 78 yards and a touchdown to lead Pitt to a thrilling victory to remain undefeated and position themselves firmly in the ACC Championship race. The Panthers figure to finally move into the top 25 this week, and the Panthers will look to lean on a defense that is 18th in the country in points allowed, averaging just 13.4 points per game to keep them in that position. 
Pitt will host North Carolina next Saturday in an effort to become bowl-eligible in the first six weeks of the season. The Panthers then go to Boston College and travel to Miami to face the ACC favorite Hurricanes, in what will be the biggest test for Greiner and the Panthers as they look to adjust after losing Heintschel.

title: Aaron Judge injury update: Yankees slugger not on ALDS roster vs. Rays - CBS Sports

body:
Judge has been on the injured list since Sept. 16 and missed New York's two-game Wild Card Series sweep over the Red Sox
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 3, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:17 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The New York Yankees won their Wild Card Series over the Boston Red Sox with relative ease, outscoring their rivals 18-2 in the two-game sweep. They did so without their biggest name and best player, three-time AL MVP Aaron Judge, and now will try to do the same in the American League Division Series.The Yankees will again not have their captain for the ALDS against the Tampa Bay Rays, beginning Saturday at Tropicana Field. Judge is not on New York's ALDS roster, the team announced Saturday morning ahead of its 6:30 p.m. game. Judge, 34, has been on the injured list since Sept. 16 with a calf strain.The only change from the Wild Card Series roster was the removal of infielder Amed Rosario and addition of reliever Ryan Weathers."Ultimately, I obviously decided keeping him off was the best thing," manager Aaron Boone told reporters on Saturday. "Again, I feel like he's getting close, but I feel like for us to get a version of Aaron back and to win a World Series, I feel like this week's important for him to continue to work towards getting back.
"He just started running. He's hit now a couple of days. So I think another several days of doing that and building some endurance, I think, is important. Understanding entirely that we're guaranteed nothing. We don't play well, next week we're home and we don't get it."
Unlike during the regular season, when players can be added to the roster at will, Judge cannot replace another player during this round, barring injury. Had the Yankees chosen to roster him and found that he could not play, removing him would have also invalidated him for the ALCS, as a player being replaced on the roster due to injury, by rule, must be left off the roster for the next round. Forcing a return now could have led to Judge missing more time down the road."In the end, I just felt like the best chance for us to get, again, a good version of Aaron was another five, six, seven days of truly building up his running, building up the endurance, getting at-bats, taking BP every day," Boone said on Saturday.
Furthermore, if Judge had served as a designated hitter instead of playing right field in the ALDS, that would have forced Luis García Jr. to the bench with Ben Rice playing first base. García has been productive since the Yankees landed him ahead of the trade deadline, and he was 3 for 5 with a home run in Game 2 of the Wild Card Series.Judge was sidelined for most of the 2026 regular season due to what was initially termed a bone bruise in his right ribcage that was also affecting his right shoulder. He returned in early September, but was only able to play in seven games before suffering a lower leg injury. As it turns out, the Yankees called the latest injury a right calf strain.In those seven games after his return from the injured list, without a minor-league rehab assignment, Judge was 4 for 23 (.174) with 13 strikeouts, though he did hit a home run in his sixth game.
In total this season, Judge appeared in 66 games, hitting .241/.360/.511 (.140 OPS+) with 10 doubles, 18 home runs, 41 RBI, 45 runs and 1.9 WAR. The Yankees were 41-25 in games Judge started this season and, now including the playoffs, are 54-43. The Rays had the best record in the AL this season at 98-64 and won the AL East by 4 ½ games over New York. The Rays won the regular-season series over the Yankees, 7-6.

title: Notre Dame earns soggy CFP style points as CJ Carr continues to quietly build Heisman case - CBS Sports
description: After an early scare, Notre Dame removed all drama with a physically dominant second half performance against Nor
body:
After an early scare, Notre Dame removed all drama with a physically dominant second half performance against North Carolina
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 3, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:58 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Perhaps Heisman voters will catch the replay of CJ Carr's five-touchdown performance in Saturday's 37-26 win at North Carolina. The Notre Dame quarterback overcame a rain-soaked ball and a high-pressure Bill Belichick scheme devised to rattle the Irish signal caller.He finished 21 of 29 for 234 yards and four touchdown passes, along with a 9-yard touchdown run on a broken fourth-down play in the red zone. Carr's only been sacked twice through five starts this season behind a nasty offensive front."These guys just want it, we play hard and we play for each other so it's a fun group to be around," Carr said. "We faced some adversity, but came out firing off (in the second half)."Carr entered as the clear-cut No. 4 in the Heisman race behind the likes of Alabama's Keelon Russell, Ohio State's Jermiah Smith and Miami's Darian Mensah. He's not flashy and rarely makes a jaw-dropping highlight, but he's the perfect triggerman for Mike Denbrock's offense and what Notre Dame needs to win a national championship this season under center.
Carr has thrown at least three touchdowns and rushed for another in three consecutive starts. He's the first Irish quarterback to accomplish that feat in 30 years.Game control mattersThe College Football Playoff selection committee won't debut its first set of rankings until Nov. 3, but Notre Dame's second-half pullaway could impact overall opinions of the Fighting Irish.The game looked uncomfortably tight after North Carolina's Jaden Jefferson ran back a kickoff for a touchdown to open the second half. Instead, Notre Dame marched down the field with a nine-minute drive capped with a fourth-down touchdown to set the tone for a dominant second half. 
The CFP selection committee uses its own metrics for evaluating teams, but analytics models such as game control and strength of record come into play.Notre Dame entered Week 5 ranked No. 6 in the country in game control ahead of Texas, Alabama, Indiana and a few other top-10 teams. Game control tracks a team's average chance of winning through each game, providing more context for how convincingly it has handled its schedule. A close win would've been detrimental to Notre Dame's resume, but what it showed instead during a steady downpour was a taking-care-of-business victory.A necessary reminder after the Fighting Irish were excluded from the 12-team bracket last season: Notre Dame receives an automatic bid if it is ranked in the CFP Top 12 on Selection Sunday this fall based on a memorandum of understanding signed by Notre Dame in spring 2025.
Notre Dame hits second gearNotre Dame rolled the dice in the second quarter, leading 21-7 and going for a knockout blow, but failed on fourth down from inside UNC's 3-yard line. The Tar Heels responded with a 97-yard scoring drive to essentially end the first half, going into the locker room with momentum while trailing by a touchdown.Notre Dame's first possession of the second half was a methodical 17-play, 75-yard drive that took more than nine minutes before the Fighting Irish followed that up with a three-and-out on defense. The Tar Heels possessed the football for only 1:28 in the third quarter, and their only semblance of rhythm after intermission came on their final possession midway through the final frame."We've got a resilient group of guys on that field with a golden helmet on and the message at halftime was to go out and dominate, stick to what we do," Carr said.
Fighting Irish's remaining schedulevs. Stanford, Oct. 10at No. 10 BYU, Oct. 17vs. Navy (Foxborough, Mass.), Oct. 21vs. No. 4 Miami, Nov. 7vs. Boston College, Nov. 14vs. No. 21 SMU, Nov. 21at SyracuseCarr's going to get three Heisman moment opportunities moving forward for the unbeaten Fighting Irish, the first coming in two weeks on the road against BYU. His outing against Miami and fellow standout quarterback Darian Mensah on Nov. 7 will provide a telling mark in the Heisman conversation coming out of the CFP's second set of rankings.
